title: Rule BL-28 as OD-24: captions are fetched as json3, VTT stays as a fallback
body:
Rules **BL-28** as **OD-24**, adding **R1013**.

**R1013:** the caption fetch requests `json3` and prefers it, reading a transcript as the concatenation of every segment of every event — **`aAppend` included**, because they carry real speech and dropping them loses 2,257 words on the measured video. Cue start times come from json3's segment timing rather than from a display frame, so a mention's `start_seconds` is the moment its own words were spoken.

WebVTT stays as the fallback for a track offering no `json3`, and its roll-up duplication is removed **on parse rather than stored**: no cached transcript may contain the same line three times whichever path produced it.

**The path taken is recorded per video and reported in the run summary**, prominently when the fallback was used — because a fallback nobody notices is a reconstruction silently mixed in with verbatim text, and a transcript reconstructed within 0.05% and one taken verbatim are both fine to use and must never be indistinguishable when a later question is asked about a specific claim's timestamp.

**What decides the format is not the size.** De-duplicating the VTT works, and it was measured: the reconstruction lands within **0.05%** of json3's text (73,121 characters against 73,159), and a conservative structural rule recovers all but **0.008%** of what an aggressive word-overlap merge would — so the version that could eat genuinely repeated speech is never needed. It was rejected as the *primary* source on two grounds: it is a reconstruction whose correctness would have to be re-proved for every video forever, and it cannot recover per-word timing the VTT never carried.

R5 cuts every excerpt window from a mention's `start_seconds`, and in roll-up VTT a board name inside a two-line frame inherits the **first** line's timestamp — up to ~2.5 seconds early. V11 makes that timestamp the thing the owner acts on; V14 makes an uncheckable recommendation unacceptable. **If the cost were unchanged this decision would still be right.**

Deleting the VTT path was also weighed and rejected: `json3` is an undocumented internal format that can change without notice, where WebVTT is a W3C standard with a parser already in the tree and under test. The fallback is what keeps an upstream format change a degraded run rather than a total outage.

Ledger entry only. The plan follows on its own pull request, then the code.
